topic.title: Variance-Reduced and Composite Stochastic Optimization
topic.overview: Many learning objectives combine a smooth loss with nonsmooth penalties, constraints, or geometric structure. This topic develops stochastic optimization methods for those settings, including proximal updates, variance reduction, momentum, and manifold-aware algorithms. A representative analysis establishes convergence to stationary points for nonsmooth nonconvex finite-sum problems using constant-size minibatches.
topic.whyItMatters: Cheap noisy updates are valuable only if their accumulated error remains controlled. Theory clarifies which assumptions permit faster convergence, what type of solution is guaranteed, and when additional computation for variance reduction or constraints is worthwhile.
topic.evolution: Earlier representatives concern regularized objectives and accelerated stochastic methods. Later work extends variance reduction to nonconvex, composite, and minimax problems. Recent directions include dependent stochastic observations, penalty methods, and Riemannian optimization for dimension reduction, adapting the update rule to the structure of the task.
openQuestions: How can methods adapt to noise and regularity without fragile tuning?
Which theoretical speedups persist when gradient and communication costs are measured together?
